items.relationship: A temperature decrease across the filter drier localizes a restriction at that component. If high superheat is also present, restricted liquid flow can explain the starved evaporator.

steps.action: Replace the restricted filter drier using proper recovery/service procedures.
steps.record: After service, run the system normally and recheck filter-drier inlet/outlet temperature, superheat, subcooling and pressures.

items.heading: Restricted filter drier indicated
items.short_meaning: A temperature drop across the drier localizes a liquid-line restriction at that component.

items.relationship: The TXV sensing bulb tells the valve about suction-line temperature. Poor contact, wrong position or poor installation can give the valve the wrong signal and contribute to incorrect refrigerant feed. If high superheat is present, correct this known TXV input problem before blaming charge or another component.

steps.action: Correct the sensing bulb contact, location and mounting per the TXV manufacturer instructions.
steps.record: Component → Metering Device → Observations → Sensing Bulb Contact / Position / Insulation.

steps.action: Run the system in Stable cooling until readings stabilize, then recheck evaporator superheat.
steps.record: If superheat remains high, continue with liquid supply and TXV inlet/equalizer checks.

items.heading: TXV sensing-bulb problem
items.short_meaning: The observed bulb problem can make the TXV control refrigerant feed incorrectly; correct it before judging charge.

items.relationship: The external equalizer supplies evaporator-outlet pressure to the TXV control mechanism. A blocked, leaking, disconnected or incorrectly connected equalizer can make the TXV control refrigerant flow incorrectly. With high superheat, this is a direct TXV-side clue that should be corrected first.

steps.action: Inspect and correct the external equalizer connection, restriction, leak or misapplication.
steps.record: Component → Metering Device → Observations → External Equalizer.

steps.action: Run the system in Stable cooling until readings stabilize, then recheck evaporator superheat.
steps.record: If superheat remains high, continue with TXV inlet liquid condition/strainer and upstream liquid-line checks.

items.heading: TXV external-equalizer problem
items.short_meaning: The observed equalizer problem can make the TXV respond to the wrong evaporator-outlet pressure.

items.relationship: A stopped condenser fan reduces condenser airflow and heat rejection and can drive condensing pressure/temperature high. The stopped fan is the immediate fault to isolate; do not diagnose charge from high head pressure until airflow is restored.

steps.action: With power safely isolated, check for a blocked blade or mechanical obstruction.
steps.record: Component → Condenser → Observations → Fan Operation.

steps.action: If mechanically free, verify the fan circuit is being commanded on and check correct supply voltage at the fan circuit using safe electrical procedures.
steps.record: Record the electrical finding in component notes until dedicated electrical fields are added.

steps.action: If the motor uses a run capacitor, test it against its rated capacitance/tolerance. If supply/control and capacitor are good, test the fan motor and wiring/control device.
steps.record: Record capacitor, motor or control finding in component notes.

steps.action: After repair, verify correct fan rotation/airflow and recheck condensing pressure/temperature.
steps.record: Measurements → condenser/high-side readings.

items.heading: Condenser fan is not running
items.short_meaning: This is a direct airflow/heat-rejection fault. Isolate why the fan is stopped before diagnosing refrigerant charge.

items.relationship: A dirty or blocked condenser reduces airflow and heat rejection. Correct this known airflow problem before using high-side readings to judge refrigerant charge.

steps.action: Clean/remove the condenser airflow restriction and confirm the fan operates normally.
steps.record: Component → Condenser → Observations → Coil Condition and Fan Operation.

steps.action: Run the system in Stable cooling until readings stabilize, then recheck condensing pressure/temperature and condenser split.
steps.record: Measurements → condenser/high-side and condenser-air readings.

items.heading: Condenser coil is dirty/restricted
items.short_meaning: This directly reduces condenser airflow and heat rejection. Correct it before interpreting high-side readings.

items.relationship: Ice restricts evaporator airflow, but icing is usually a result that still needs a cause. Start with airflow and defrost evidence before moving to refrigerant-side causes.

steps.action: First check whether the evaporator fan is running normally and whether the air path is blocked.
steps.record: Component → Evaporator → Observations → Fan Operation and Coil Condition.

steps.action: If fan/airflow are normal, check defrost operation and termination, then door openings/air infiltration and drain/heater issues as applicable.
steps.record: Use the relevant component observations/notes; dedicated defrost-control fields are used where available.

steps.action: After the coil is clear and airflow/defrost problems are corrected, run Stable cooling and recheck temperatures, pressures and superheat before judging refrigerant feed.
steps.record: Measurements → evaporator and refrigerant readings.

items.heading: Evaporator coil is iced
items.short_meaning: Icing restricts airflow, but the cause still must be isolated. Start with fan/airflow and defrost evidence.

items.heading: Evaporator fan is not running
items.short_meaning: This is a direct evaporator-airflow fault. Find why the fan is stopped before using refrigerant readings to diagnose charge or the TXV.
items.relationship: A stopped evaporator fan reduces heat transfer and can contribute to poor cooling and coil icing. Isolate the fan circuit/mechanical fault first; refrigeration readings can be misleading while airflow is abnormal.

steps.action: With power safely isolated, check whether the fan blade/motor turns freely and whether ice or another obstruction is blocking it.
steps.record: Component → Evaporator → Observations → Fan Operation / Airflow / Coil Condition.

steps.action: If mechanically free, determine whether the fan should be commanded on, then verify the correct supply voltage at the fan circuit using safe electrical procedures.
steps.record: Use the evaporator/component notes for the electrical result until dedicated fan-electrical fields are added.

steps.action: If correct voltage is present, check the motor circuit. If this motor uses a run capacitor, test capacitance against its rating/tolerance; then check the motor and wiring. If voltage is absent, trace the fan control/relay, fan-delay/defrost control and wiring.
steps.record: Record capacitor, motor, relay/control or wiring finding in component notes.

steps.action: After repair, verify fan rotation and airflow. Clear/defrost an iced coil as required, then run normal cooling and recheck box temperature and refrigeration measurements.
steps.record: Component → Evaporator observations; Measurements → evaporator/refrigerant readings.

items.heading: Evaporator airflow is restricted
items.short_meaning: Correct the known airflow problem before using suction pressure or superheat to diagnose a refrigerant-side fault.
items.relationship: Low evaporator airflow reduces heat load on the coil and changes suction pressure, temperature difference and superheat behavior.

steps.action: Check for an iced/dirty coil, blocked return/discharge path, fan problem or other physical airflow restriction.
steps.record: Component → Evaporator → Observations → Airflow / Coil Condition / Fan Operation.

steps.action: Correct the airflow restriction, then run normal cooling until readings stabilize and recheck temperatures, suction pressure and superheat.
steps.record: Measurements → evaporator and suction readings.

items.heading: Liquid-line solenoid is not opening / passing flow
items.short_meaning: This can stop or reduce liquid refrigerant feed to the evaporator. Separate an electrical command/coil problem from a mechanical valve problem.
items.relationship: When cooling calls for liquid flow, a solenoid that does not open can starve the evaporator and cause low suction/high superheat symptoms.

steps.action: Confirm there is a cooling demand and that the solenoid is commanded open.
steps.record: System Check → Room / control evidence → Cooling Demand / Solenoid Command.

steps.action: Check the specified voltage at the solenoid coil. No voltage points upstream to control/wiring; correct voltage with no opening points toward the coil/valve/mechanical path.
steps.record: Record voltage/coil finding in Solenoid notes until a dedicated voltage field is added.

steps.action: After correction, verify the valve opens and liquid flow/feed returns, then recheck suction pressure and superheat.
steps.record: Component → Solenoid observations; Measurements → evaporator/suction.

items.heading: Liquid-line solenoid is not closing
items.short_meaning: A solenoid that continues to pass refrigerant when commanded closed can prevent normal pump-down and can contribute to off-cycle refrigerant migration/floodback.
items.relationship: Separate a control-command problem from a leaking/stuck valve by comparing command, coil voltage and actual refrigerant flow.

steps.action: Confirm the solenoid is commanded closed and determine whether coil voltage is removed as designed.
steps.record: System Check → Room / control evidence → Solenoid Command / Flow.

steps.action: If the command/voltage is correct but flow continues, inspect the valve for a stuck plunger, debris or damaged/leaking seat. If command is wrong, trace thermostat/controller/wiring.
steps.record: Component → Solenoid observations/notes.

steps.action: After correction, verify normal pump-down/off-cycle behavior before evaluating remaining refrigeration symptoms.
steps.record: Operating State / control evidence and suction pressure.

items.heading: Compressor is not running
items.short_meaning: First determine whether the compressor is supposed to run, then separate a control/power problem from a starting-component, overload or compressor problem.
items.relationship: A stopped compressor is not by itself proof of compressor failure. Cooling demand, safeties, contactor, terminal voltage, overload/start components and the compressor must be isolated in order.

steps.action: Confirm there is a cooling call and that the compressor is not intentionally off because of defrost, pump-down, satisfied control or anti-short-cycle delay.
steps.record: System Check → Operating State and Room / control evidence.

steps.action: If it should be running, follow the wiring diagram and check safeties/control output, contactor coil and contactor output.
steps.record: System Check → Room / control evidence.

steps.action: Verify correct voltage at the compressor terminals. If voltage is absent, trace the upstream control/power path. If correct voltage is present but it will not start, check overload and manufacturer-specified start/run components before condemning the compressor.
steps.record: Compressor/control observations and notes.

steps.action: After repair, verify compressor starts, establishes normal suction/discharge pressure separation and operates within its approved envelope.
steps.record: Measurements → suction/high-side; compressor observations.

items.heading: High-pressure safety is open/tripped
items.short_meaning: Do not simply reset and run. Find the cause of excessive condensing pressure first.
items.relationship: Common branches include condenser airflow/dirty coil/fan failure, excessive refrigerant, non-condensables and control problems.

steps.action: With the system safe, inspect condenser coil condition and verify condenser fan/airflow before considering charge-related causes.
steps.record: Component → Condenser → Coil Condition / Fan Operation / Airflow.

steps.action: If heat rejection is normal, use stabilized high-side pressure/temperature, applicable subcooling/receiver information and service history to evaluate overcharge, non-condensables or head-pressure control issues.
steps.record: Measurements → condenser/high-side; System Check → control evidence.

items.heading: Defrost / ice-removal problem indicated
items.short_meaning: Determine whether heat is produced, defrost runs long enough, termination is correct and melt water drains without refreezing.
items.relationship: Persistent evaporator ice can come from failed defrost heat, incorrect schedule/termination, drain refreeze, fan/control problems or excess moisture infiltration.

steps.action: Verify the defrost command/schedule and whether the defrost heat source actually operates.
steps.record: Defrost/control observations and notes.

steps.action: Verify termination sensor/control and inspect drain pan, drain line and drain heater for refreezing.
steps.record: Defrost/control observations and notes.

steps.action: After the coil is fully clear, verify fan delay/airflow and door sealing, then return to normal cooling and recheck performance.
steps.record: Evaporator and room/control observations.

items.heading: Bubbles / flashing observed in the liquid-line sight glass
items.short_meaning: This is a liquid-supply clue, not a charge diagnosis by itself. Determine whether the liquid is flashing from low inventory, pressure drop/restriction or inadequate subcooling.
items.relationship: Bubbles can accompany inadequate liquid supply but must be interpreted with receiver configuration, subcooling, pressure drop and localized liquid-line evidence.

steps.action: Check liquid-line temperature/pressure evidence for a restriction, especially across the filter drier and other liquid-line components.
steps.record: Measurements → before/after filter drier and liquid line.

steps.action: Check applicable subcooling/liquid condition and look for leak/charge evidence before adding refrigerant.
steps.record: Measurements → condenser/liquid line; Component observations → oil/leak evidence.

items.heading: Evaporator is underfed / high superheat
items.short_meaning: High superheat shows inadequate evaporator feed, but does not identify the cause by itself.
items.relationship: Separate low refrigerant inventory from upstream liquid-line restriction and TXV/EEV underfeeding with the next available liquid-side check.

steps.action: If the system is in stable cooling, check the liquid-supply side next: applicable subcooling/liquid condition, filter-drier temperature/pressure drop, sight glass and TXV inlet condition. Use the first check not already completed.
steps.record: Measurements and Component observations.

steps.action: Use localized evidence to separate low inventory, liquid-line restriction and TXV/EEV underfeeding; do not add refrigerant from high superheat alone.
steps.record: System Check will reevaluate as each result is entered.

items.relationship: A wet moisture indicator supports moisture contamination in the liquid line; confirm the indicator is valid and address dehydration rather than treating it as a charge indication.

steps.action: Confirm the indicator condition and service history, then address moisture contamination using proper refrigeration service procedures and an appropriate filter drier.
steps.record: Record the result in the applicable component observation/notes and rerun System Check.

items.heading: Moisture is indicated in the liquid line
items.short_meaning: A wet moisture indicator supports moisture contamination in the liquid line; confirm the indicator is valid and address dehydration rather than treating it as a charge indication.

items.relationship: TXV hunting means refrigerant feed is unstable. Check load stability, bulb mounting, liquid supply and valve application before adjusting or replacing the valve.

steps.action: Confirm stable cooling/load first; inspect sensing-bulb mounting and liquid supply to the TXV, then observe superheat stability.
steps.record: Record the result in the applicable component observation/notes and rerun System Check.

items.heading: TXV hunting / unstable feed
items.short_meaning: TXV hunting means refrigerant feed is unstable. Check load stability, bulb mounting, liquid supply and valve application before adjusting or replacing the valve.

items.relationship: Warm humid air entering the box adds sensible and latent load and can contribute to poor temperature control and evaporator frost.

steps.action: Correct the open door, gasket, closer or other infiltration source; allow the box to recover, then reassess temperature and refrigeration readings.
steps.record: Record the result in the applicable component observation/notes and rerun System Check.

items.heading: Door / infiltration load confirmed
items.short_meaning: Warm humid air entering the box adds sensible and latent load and can contribute to poor temperature control and evaporator frost.

items.relationship: A large warm product load can cause long run time and temporarily elevated box temperature without proving a refrigeration fault.

steps.action: Allow/monitor pull-down and trend room/product temperature before refrigerant changes; investigate refrigeration capacity only if temperature stops improving or operating limits are exceeded.
steps.record: Record the result in the applicable component observation/notes and rerun System Check.

items.heading: High warm-product load confirmed
items.short_meaning: A large warm product load can cause long run time and temporarily elevated box temperature without proving a refrigeration fault.

items.relationship: A sensor that disagrees with a trusted reference can mislead the controller and diagnostic interpretation.

steps.action: Verify sensor placement, calibration and wiring against a trusted temperature reference before changing refrigeration settings.
steps.record: Record the result in the applicable component observation/notes and rerun System Check.

items.heading: Room temperature sensor reading is suspect
items.short_meaning: A sensor that disagrees with a trusted reference can mislead the controller and diagnostic interpretation.

items.relationship: Cooling demand is present but the contactor coil is not energized, so the control/safety circuit must be traced upstream.

steps.action: Verify control voltage through thermostat/controller, safeties and interlocks to the contactor coil; find where voltage is lost.
steps.record: Record the result in the applicable component observation/notes and rerun System Check.

items.heading: Contactor coil is not energized
items.short_meaning: Cooling demand is present but the contactor coil is not energized, so the control/safety circuit must be traced upstream.

items.relationship: The contactor is commanded/energized but proper output voltage is not reaching the load.

steps.action: With safe electrical procedures, verify line voltage into and out of the contactor; inspect contacts/connections and correct the failed power path.
steps.record: Record the result in the applicable component observation/notes and rerun System Check.

items.heading: Contactor is not passing power
items.short_meaning: The contactor is commanded/energized but proper output voltage is not reaching the load.

items.relationship: An open fuse interrupts the power circuit; the cause must be found before simply replacing it.

steps.action: De-energize safely, inspect for shorts/ground faults or failed loads, correct the cause, replace with the specified fuse, then verify current and operation.
steps.record: Record the result in the applicable component observation/notes and rerun System Check.

items.heading: Open/blown fuse found
items.short_meaning: An open fuse interrupts the power circuit; the cause must be found before simply replacing it.

items.relationship: An open overload indicates compressor protection has operated; overheating, electrical problems or excessive load must be investigated before restart.

steps.action: Allow safe cooling as required, then check supply voltage/current, condenser conditions, start components and compressor mechanical/electrical condition before resetting/restarting.
steps.record: Record the result in the applicable component observation/notes and rerun System Check.

items.heading: Compressor overload is open / compressor hot
items.short_meaning: An open overload indicates compressor protection has operated; overheating, electrical problems or excessive load must be investigated before restart.

items.relationship: A deliberate anti-short-cycle delay can keep the compressor off even when cooling demand is present.

steps.action: Verify the delay timing and control sequence. If the compressor starts after the specified delay, do not diagnose a compressor fault.
steps.record: Record the result in the applicable component observation/notes and rerun System Check.

items.heading: Anti-short-cycle delay is active
items.short_meaning: A deliberate anti-short-cycle delay can keep the compressor off even when cooling demand is present.

items.relationship: An open low-pressure control can be normal at the end of pump-down; interpret it with operating state and solenoid command before calling it a fault.

steps.action: Confirm operating/pump-down state and liquid-line solenoid command. During cooling, compare actual suction pressure and LP cut-in/cutout with the application setting/specification; inspect the sensing line and control calibration before adjustment or replacement. If pump-down is complete, verify the compressor stops and restarts at the intended pressures.
steps.record: Record the result in the applicable component observation/notes and rerun System Check.

items.heading: Low-pressure control is open
items.short_meaning: An open low-pressure control can be normal at the end of pump-down; interpret it with operating state and solenoid command before calling it a fault.

items.relationship: The valve is commanded open but flow is not established, indicating a coil/voltage, valve, or upstream liquid-supply problem.

steps.action: Verify correct coil voltage and magnetism, then check valve opening and upstream liquid supply/restriction.
steps.record: Record the result in the applicable component observation/notes and rerun System Check.

items.heading: Solenoid commanded open but no refrigerant flow
items.short_meaning: The valve is commanded open but flow is not established, indicating a coil/voltage, valve, or upstream liquid-supply problem.

items.relationship: Continued flow with a close command indicates the valve may be leaking, stuck open, or still electrically energized.

steps.action: Verify coil voltage is removed on the close command; if de-energized and flow continues, inspect/service the valve for a stuck or leaking seat.
steps.record: Record the result in the applicable component observation/notes and rerun System Check.

items.heading: Solenoid commanded closed but flow continues
items.short_meaning: Continued flow with a close command indicates the valve may be leaking, stuck open, or still electrically energized.

items.relationship: Drain ice points to a drainage or defrost-water removal problem and can contribute to recurring evaporator icing.

steps.action: Inspect and clear the drain, trap and drain heater if used; verify defrost water drains freely and then confirm the coil completes defrost.
steps.record: Record the result in the applicable component observation/notes and rerun System Check.

items.heading: Evaporator drain / drain-pan ice present
items.short_meaning: Drain ice points to a drainage or defrost-water removal problem and can contribute to recurring evaporator icing.

items.relationship: A starved evaporator with retained liquid on the high side favors restricted liquid feed over simple undercharge.

steps.action: Check filter drier temperature/pressure drop, liquid-line solenoid and TXV inlet/strainer to localize the restriction.
steps.record: Record the result in the applicable measurement/component/control field and rerun System Check.

items.heading: Liquid-line or metering restriction is favored
items.short_meaning: A starved evaporator with retained liquid on the high side favors restricted liquid feed over simple undercharge.

items.relationship: High condensing pressure plus high subcooling with verified condenser airflow makes excess liquid inventory a stronger possibility, but charge method, receiver condition and noncondensables still matter.

steps.action: Verify receiver/charge condition and rule out noncondensables and head-pressure-control problems before recovering refrigerant.
steps.record: Record the result in the applicable measurement/component/control field and rerun System Check.

items.heading: Overcharge / excess liquid inventory is possible
items.short_meaning: High condensing pressure plus high subcooling with verified condenser airflow makes excess liquid inventory a stronger possibility, but charge method, receiver condition and noncondensables still matter.

items.relationship: High ambient raises the condensing requirement even when condenser airflow is normal.

steps.action: Verify condenser split/CTOA against the application target and confirm there is no hot-air recirculation before judging charge.
steps.record: Record the result in the applicable measurement/component/control field and rerun System Check.

items.heading: High ambient / heat-rejection load is a major contributor
items.short_meaning: High ambient raises the condensing requirement even when condenser airflow is normal.

items.relationship: A reduced pressure differential can indicate compressor inefficiency, but load, bypass/unloader conditions and operating state must be checked first.

steps.action: Confirm stable load and compressor operation, then evaluate compression ratio, current and compressor capacity against manufacturer data.
steps.record: Record the result in the applicable measurement/component/control field and rerun System Check.

items.heading: Compressor inefficiency / low compression is possible
items.short_meaning: A reduced pressure differential can indicate compressor inefficiency, but load, bypass/unloader conditions and operating state must be checked first.

items.relationship: Both suction and condensing pressure are low; low load, low ambient/head-pressure control and insufficient evaporator feed are competing explanations.

steps.action: Check box/load condition, ambient/head-pressure control and evaporator feed evidence such as superheat, subcooling and liquid condition.
steps.record: Record the result in the applicable measurement/component/control field and rerun System Check.

items.heading: Low load / low ambient / insufficient feed must be separated
items.short_meaning: Both suction and condensing pressure are low; low load, low ambient/head-pressure control and insufficient evaporator feed are competing explanations.

items.relationship: Low superheat means vapor leaving the evaporator has little margin above saturation and may indicate overfeeding or floodback risk.

steps.action: Verify measurement accuracy and stable load/airflow, then check TXV bulb/setting, valve seat/size and load before adjusting the valve.
steps.record: Record the result in the applicable measurement/component/control field and rerun System Check.

items.heading: Evaporator overfeeding / floodback risk
items.short_meaning: Low superheat means vapor leaving the evaporator has little margin above saturation and may indicate overfeeding or floodback risk.

items.relationship: Low condensing pressure can reduce liquid pressure/subcooling margin and contribute to flashing; bubbles do not by themselves prove low charge.

steps.action: Check ambient/head-pressure control and liquid-line pressure drop/subcooling before making a charge decision.
steps.record: Record the result in the applicable measurement/component/control field and rerun System Check.

items.heading: Low condensing pressure can contribute to sight-glass flashing
items.short_meaning: Low condensing pressure can reduce liquid pressure/subcooling margin and contribute to flashing; bubbles do not by themselves prove low charge.

items.relationship: High superheat, low subcooling and high condensing pressure do not cleanly support one simple charge fault.

steps.action: Verify operating state and measurement validity, then check condenser airflow/ambient and localized liquid-line restriction before adjusting charge.
steps.record: Record the result in the applicable measurement/component/control field and rerun System Check.

items.heading: Evidence is conflicting; do not force a charge diagnosis
items.short_meaning: High superheat, low subcooling and high condensing pressure do not cleanly support one simple charge fault.

items.relationship: A stopped compressor can be normal when there is no cooling demand; verify the control state before troubleshooting the compressor circuit.

steps.action: Verify box temperature, setpoint and controller state, then verify compressor operation on the next legitimate cooling call.
steps.record: Record the result in the applicable measurement/component/control field and rerun System Check.

items.heading: System may be satisfied / no cooling call
items.short_meaning: A stopped compressor can be normal when there is no cooling demand; verify the control state before troubleshooting the compressor circuit.

items.relationship: A large warm product load can legitimately keep the compressor running during pull-down.

steps.action: Confirm pull-down progress, airflow and operating limits; investigate refrigeration capacity only if temperature stops improving or limits are exceeded.
steps.record: Record the result in the applicable measurement/component/control field and rerun System Check.

items.heading: Heavy pull-down load may explain long runtime
items.short_meaning: A large warm product load can legitimately keep the compressor running during pull-down.

items.relationship: Continuous compressor operation while the room fails to reach setpoint requires systematic load, airflow, feed and capacity checks.

steps.action: Check room/load and evaporator airflow first, then condenser airflow, refrigerant feed/TXV behavior and compressor capacity.
steps.record: Record the result in the applicable measurement/component/control field and rerun System Check.

items.heading: Cooling capacity problem requires systematic checks
items.short_meaning: Continuous compressor operation while the room fails to reach setpoint requires systematic load, airflow, feed and capacity checks.

items.relationship: The direct condenser-airflow fault can cause high head and must be corrected before charge is judged.

steps.action: Repair/restore condenser fan first; then stabilize and reassess head pressure, subcooling and receiver/charge condition.
steps.record: Record the result in the applicable measurement/component/control field and rerun System Check.

items.heading: Condenser fan failure is the first priority
items.short_meaning: The direct condenser-airflow fault can cause high head and must be corrected before charge is judged.

items.relationship: Both evaporator icing and a dirty/restricted condenser are confirmed; refrigeration readings will not represent normal operation until these faults are corrected.

steps.action: Address the evaporator icing cause/airflow and condenser cleanliness, then run stable cooling and collect fresh readings.
steps.record: Record the result in the applicable measurement/component/control field and rerun System Check.

items.heading: Multiple heat-transfer faults are present
items.short_meaning: Both evaporator icing and a dirty/restricted condenser are confirmed; refrigeration readings will not represent normal operation until these faults are corrected.

items.relationship: Compressor-off is expected without a cooling call, while the dirty condenser is a separate heat-rejection maintenance issue.

steps.action: Clean/correct the condenser as needed and verify compressor operation on the next legitimate cooling call.
steps.record: Record the result in the applicable measurement/component/control field and rerun System Check.

items.heading: No compressor fault is established; condenser maintenance finding remains
items.short_meaning: Compressor-off is expected without a cooling call, while the dirty condenser is a separate heat-rejection maintenance issue.

items.relationship: Both TXV sensing inputs can cause incorrect valve feed and must be corrected before charge or valve-replacement decisions.

steps.action: Correct bulb installation and external-equalizer condition, then stabilize and recheck superheat.
steps.record: Record the result in the applicable measurement/component/control field and rerun System Check.

items.heading: Multiple TXV input problems are present
items.short_meaning: Both TXV sensing inputs can cause incorrect valve feed and must be corrected before charge or valve-replacement decisions.

items.relationship: Ice restricts evaporator airflow/load and can drive suction abnormal; refrigerant diagnosis is unreliable until the coil is clear and the icing cause is corrected.

steps.action: Diagnose/correct the icing cause, clear the coil, then stabilize and remeasure suction pressure and superheat.
steps.record: Record the result in the applicable measurement/component/control field and rerun System Check.

items.heading: Icing / airflow must be resolved before suction diagnosis
items.short_meaning: Ice restricts evaporator airflow/load and can drive suction abnormal; refrigerant diagnosis is unreliable until the coil is clear and the icing cause is corrected.

items.relationship: A closed/non-opening solenoid can directly restrict liquid feed and cause low suction/starvation.

steps.action: Troubleshoot solenoid command, voltage and valve operation first; after restoring flow, recheck suction pressure and superheat.
steps.record: Record the result in the applicable measurement/component/control field and rerun System Check.

items.heading: Liquid-line solenoid fault explains starvation direction
items.short_meaning: A closed/non-opening solenoid can directly restrict liquid feed and cause low suction/starvation.

items.relationship: High load can raise suction while low head may reflect ambient/head-control conditions; compressor inefficiency is not proven.

steps.action: Check ambient/head-pressure control and compressor differential/current while tracking pull-down before condemning the compressor.
steps.record: Record the result in the applicable measurement/component/control field and rerun System Check.

items.heading: Load context must be separated from compressor inefficiency
items.short_meaning: High load can raise suction while low head may reflect ambient/head-control conditions; compressor inefficiency is not proven.

items.relationship: After a long off-cycle or uncertain startup condition, compressor heat alone does not identify a failed compressor; migration/floodback and crankcase protection must be considered.

steps.action: Before condemning the compressor, verify crankcase heater operation, off-cycle conditions, oil condition and startup behavior.
steps.record: Record off-cycle duration, crankcase heater status, oil condition and startup suction/superheat behavior.

items.heading: Refrigerant migration / startup floodback risk must be considered
items.short_meaning: After a long off-cycle or uncertain startup condition, compressor heat alone does not identify a failed compressor; migration/floodback and crankcase protection must be considered.

items.relationship: Low superheat during post-defrost recovery can be transient and can increase liquid-return risk; it is not steady-cooling charge evidence.

steps.action: Allow controlled post-defrost recovery; verify fan delay, superheat and liquid return before judging charge.
steps.record: After normal fan release and stable cooling, remeasure superheat.

items.heading: Post-defrost liquid return / floodback risk
items.short_meaning: Low superheat during post-defrost recovery can be transient and can increase liquid-return risk; it is not steady-cooling charge evidence.

items.relationship: A running compressor with weak pressure separation indicates reduced pumping performance, but load, feed and measurement accuracy must be verified before condemnation.

steps.action: Verify load, airflow, feed and measurement accuracy, then compare suction/discharge performance with model data before condemning compressor.
steps.record: Record stabilized suction/discharge pressures, current and applicable manufacturer performance data.

items.heading: Compressor pumping efficiency is suspect
items.short_meaning: A running compressor with weak pressure separation indicates reduced pumping performance, but load, feed and measurement accuracy must be verified before condemnation.

items.relationship: Weak pressure separation plus internal valve-leakage evidence strongly localizes reduced compressor pumping capacity.

steps.action: Confirm electrical/load conditions and model performance, then plan compressor repair/replacement per manufacturer procedure.
steps.record: Record pressure differential, current and leakage evidence.

items.heading: Internal compressor leakage strongly indicated
items.short_meaning: Weak pressure separation plus internal valve-leakage evidence strongly localizes reduced compressor pumping capacity.

items.relationship: An open overload protects the hot compressor. Low superheat is a floodback clue, but voltage/current and cooling conditions also require verification.

steps.action: Let protection reset safely, then diagnose floodback, voltage/current and cooling conditions before restart.
steps.record: Do not repeatedly reset protection without correcting the cause.

items.heading: Protection trip; root cause still unresolved
items.short_meaning: An open overload protects the hot compressor. Low superheat is a floodback clue, but voltage/current and cooling conditions also require verification.

items.relationship: High discharge temperature with low evaporating condition and high superheat is consistent with a starved/high-compression-ratio operating condition.

steps.action: Find the starvation cause and restore proper suction conditions before extended operation.
steps.record: Check liquid supply, restrictions, metering device and load; then recheck discharge temperature.

items.heading: High discharge-temperature risk with starved evaporator
items.short_meaning: High discharge temperature with low evaporating condition and high superheat is consistent with a starved/high-compression-ratio operating condition.

items.relationship: High condensing pressure increases compressor work and can raise current. Correct the high-side cause before judging the compressor electrically.

steps.action: Correct high-head cause first, then recheck current against nameplate/model limits.
steps.record: Verify condenser airflow, ambient/load, charge method and high-side controls.

items.heading: High compressor load associated with high condensing pressure
items.short_meaning: High condensing pressure increases compressor work and can raise current. Correct the high-side cause before judging the compressor electrically.

items.relationship: When condenser airflow is verified normal, high head requires charge/inventory, noncondensables, load/ambient and pressure-control discrimination rather than more airflow work.

steps.action: Use applicable charge method and pressure-temperature evidence to separate overcharge from noncondensables/high load.
steps.record: Record subcooling/inventory evidence, ambient/load and service history.

items.heading: High head remains after airflow causes are excluded
items.short_meaning: When condenser airflow is verified normal, high head requires charge/inventory, noncondensables, load/ambient and pressure-control discrimination rather than more airflow work.

items.relationship: High head with verified noncondensable pressure-temperature/service evidence and normal airflow localizes a refrigerant-circuit contamination problem.

steps.action: Recover/handle refrigerant according to service procedure, evacuate properly, recharge correctly, and verify.
steps.record: Verify airflow and service history before opening the circuit.

items.heading: Noncondensables strongly supported
items.short_meaning: High head with verified noncondensable pressure-temperature/service evidence and normal airflow localizes a refrigerant-circuit contamination problem.

items.relationship: High head plus direct excess-inventory/charge evidence supports overcharge after airflow causes are excluded.

steps.action: Correct charge by the equipment-specific method and verify stable operation.
steps.record: Use manufacturer charge method; do not rely on a generic target where not applicable.

items.heading: Excess refrigerant charge strongly supported
items.short_meaning: High head plus direct excess-inventory/charge evidence supports overcharge after airflow causes are excluded.

items.relationship: High superheat remains after proper liquid at the TXV and no upstream restriction are verified, so metering-device control/application becomes the next discriminator.

steps.action: Test TXV response, bulb/equalizer and application match before adjustment/replacement.
steps.record: Record bulb contact/position, equalizer condition, valve response and refrigerant/valve match.

items.heading: Metering-device underfeed becomes more likely
items.short_meaning: High superheat remains after proper liquid at the TXV and no upstream restriction are verified, so metering-device control/application becomes the next discriminator.

items.relationship: High superheat with proper inlet liquid and a failed valve response test localizes the fault to TXV control/valve behavior after bulb/equalizer verification.

steps.action: Verify bulb/equalizer one last time, then service/replace the TXV per manufacturer guidance.
steps.record: Do not change charge to compensate for a localized valve-response fault.

items.heading: TXV valve/power-element fault strongly indicated
items.short_meaning: High superheat with proper inlet liquid and a failed valve response test localizes the fault to TXV control/valve behavior after bulb/equalizer verification.

items.relationship: A valve/refrigerant application mismatch can underfeed the evaporator and cannot be corrected reliably by charge or arbitrary adjustment.

steps.action: Correct the valve/refrigerant application match before tuning or charge changes.
steps.record: Verify valve model, refrigerant, capacity and application.

items.heading: Expansion-device application mismatch
items.short_meaning: A valve/refrigerant application mismatch can underfeed the evaporator and cannot be corrected reliably by charge or arbitrary adjustment.

items.relationship: Low superheat plus abnormal TXV response requires bulb/equalizer and valve-mechanical verification before adjustment.

steps.action: Verify bulb/equalizer and valve mechanics before adjustment or replacement.
steps.record: Stabilize and remeasure superheat after correction.

items.heading: Overfeed with abnormal valve response
items.short_meaning: Low superheat plus abnormal TXV response requires bulb/equalizer and valve-mechanical verification before adjustment.

items.relationship: A sensor/transducer error can command incorrect EEV feed and must be corrected before condemning refrigerant charge or the valve.

steps.action: Verify transducer range/type, temperature sensor type/location/wiring, then reevaluate valve behavior.
steps.record: Compare sensor/transducer values with trusted references.

items.heading: Electronic superheat-control input error possible
items.short_meaning: A sensor/transducer error can command incorrect EEV feed and must be corrected before condemning refrigerant charge or the valve.

items.relationship: Incorrect sensing-bulb contact/location can produce an incorrect control signal; correct this known input fault before diagnosing the valve or charge.

steps.action: Correct bulb location/contact/insulation, stabilize system, then remeasure SH.
steps.record: Use manufacturer bulb mounting guidance.

items.heading: Bulb installation must be corrected before valve diagnosis
items.short_meaning: Incorrect sensing-bulb contact/location can produce an incorrect control signal; correct this known input fault before diagnosing the valve or charge.

items.relationship: A defrost command and proper voltage with no heater current/heat localizes an open heater/load circuit or connection.

steps.action: De-energize safely and test heater continuity/resistance and connections; repair then verify current/heat.
steps.record: Use safe electrical procedures and verify the full defrost cycle after repair.

items.heading: Defrost heater circuit/load failure localized
items.short_meaning: A defrost command and proper voltage with no heater current/heat localizes an open heater/load circuit or connection.

items.relationship: Incorrect fan release after defrost is a sequence/control fault and should be corrected before judging refrigeration readings.

steps.action: Verify fan-delay sensor/timer/controller logic and correct before evaluating refrigeration performance.
steps.record: Record actual fan release temperature/time versus equipment sequence.

items.heading: Evaporator fan-delay/control fault
items.short_meaning: Incorrect fan release after defrost is a sequence/control fault and should be corrected before judging refrigeration readings.

items.relationship: An active fan delay immediately after defrost can be normal equipment sequence, not a fan failure.

steps.action: Verify delay matches equipment sequence; wait for normal release before diagnosing fan failure.
steps.record: Confirm fan starts when the release condition is met.

items.heading: Post-defrost fan delay is intentional
items.short_meaning: An active fan delay immediately after defrost can be normal equipment sequence, not a fan failure.

items.relationship: Pressure, superheat and subcooling readings during active defrost are not ordinary stable-cooling evidence.

steps.action: Complete defrost and recovery, then obtain stabilized cooling readings.
steps.record: Do not diagnose charge from defrost readings.

items.heading: Defrost readings are not steady-cooling diagnostic evidence
items.short_meaning: Pressure, superheat and subcooling readings during active defrost are not ordinary stable-cooling evidence.

items.relationship: If the coil still ices while defrost completes and the evaporator fan operates, investigate moisture/load/drain and refrigerant-feed causes rather than replacing proven defrost hardware.

steps.action: Check door/infiltration, drain/refreeze pattern, load and refrigerant feed.
steps.record: Record frost pattern and when icing returns.

items.heading: Look beyond defrost hardware
items.short_meaning: If the coil still ices while defrost completes and the evaporator fan operates, investigate moisture/load/drain and refrigerant-feed causes rather than replacing proven defrost hardware.

items.relationship: Low evaporator load can depress evaporating conditions and contribute to icing even with the fan running.

steps.action: Confirm controls/setpoint/load, defrost performance and stable evaporating condition before charge changes.
steps.record: Do not add refrigerant solely because suction is low under low load.

items.heading: Low load may contribute to low evaporating condition/icing
items.short_meaning: Low evaporator load can depress evaporating conditions and contribute to icing even with the fan running.

items.relationship: Cooling demand with a dead contactor coil does not identify the failed upstream device when the control scheme is unknown.

steps.action: Use the equipment wiring diagram to trace control voltage through safeties and controls to the coil.
steps.record: Record the first point where control voltage is lost.

items.heading: Control circuit must be traced before component replacement
items.short_meaning: Cooling demand with a dead contactor coil does not identify the failed upstream device when the control scheme is unknown.

items.relationship: A warm box with an open LP control requires comparison of actual pressure and cutout/cutin settings with the intended control sequence.

steps.action: Compare cutout/cutin with equipment requirements and actual pressure; correct setting only per manufacturer design.
steps.record: Verify whether the control is intended for pump-down, safety, or temperature control.

items.heading: Low-pressure control setting/sequence needs verification
items.short_meaning: A warm box with an open LP control requires comparison of actual pressure and cutout/cutin settings with the intended control sequence.

items.relationship: When refrigeration performance is verified normal but the room remains warm, investigate load, infiltration, sensing/control and equipment capacity.

steps.action: Characterize load/infiltration, verify sensor/setpoint, and compare capacity with actual load.
steps.record: Avoid refrigerant adjustments without refrigeration-side evidence.

items.heading: Investigate load/control/sizing rather than refrigeration circuit
items.short_meaning: When refrigeration performance is verified normal but the room remains warm, investigate load, infiltration, sensing/control and equipment capacity.

items.relationship: When actual/design load exceeds available equipment capacity after normal airflow/feed/controls are verified, the problem is capacity/sizing rather than refrigerant charge.

steps.action: Reduce load or correct equipment sizing/capacity; verify design assumptions.
steps.record: Document actual load and equipment rated capacity.

items.heading: System capacity is insufficient for verified load
items.short_meaning: When actual/design load exceeds available equipment capacity after normal airflow/feed/controls are verified, the problem is capacity/sizing rather than refrigerant charge.

items.relationship: A dirty condenser, sensor error and high product load are independent active contributors; preserve all three while prioritizing direct corrective work.

steps.action: Correct the direct condenser restriction, validate sensor/control, characterize load, then reassess refrigeration readings.
steps.record: Do not drop the sensor or load finding after selecting the condenser as first action.

items.heading: Multiple independent contributors are active
items.short_meaning: A dirty condenser, sensor error and high product load are independent active contributors; preserve all three while prioritizing direct corrective work.

items.relationship: High SH and low SC can resemble low inventory, but a localized drier temperature drop is direct restriction evidence and must be corrected/verified first.

steps.action: Correct/verify the drier restriction, then stabilize and reassess charge using an applicable method.
steps.record: Do not add refrigerant before resolving the localized restriction evidence.

items.heading: Localized restriction outranks generic charge pattern
items.short_meaning: High SH and low SC can resemble low inventory, but a localized drier temperature drop is direct restriction evidence and must be corrected/verified first.

items.relationship: A low subcooling number against a non-applicable reference does not establish low charge, especially where receiver/configuration and measurement location affect interpretation.

steps.action: Verify measurement location and use the applicable equipment/model charging method; then check liquid condition, sight glass, leak and restriction evidence before judging charge.
steps.record: Do not add refrigerant solely from a generic subcooling target.

items.heading: Low subcooling needs configuration-aware interpretation
items.short_meaning: A low subcooling number against a non-applicable reference does not establish low charge, especially where receiver/configuration and measurement location affect interpretation.

items.relationship: An applicable manufacturer/model target takes precedence over a generic rule of thumb.

steps.action: Compare the measured value with the applicable model target and manufacturer charging procedure, then reassess charge from that target.
steps.record: Do not use the generic target when an applicable model target exists.

items.heading: Use the model-specific charging target
items.short_meaning: An applicable manufacturer/model target takes precedence over a generic rule of thumb.

items.relationship: Reasonable suction and head for the current state/load shift attention toward airflow, infiltration/load, sensing/controls and available capacity.

steps.action: Verify evaporator airflow, door/product load, sensor/control accuracy and actual capacity before opening or adjusting the refrigerant circuit.
steps.record: Do not add refrigerant simply because the room is warm.

items.heading: Warm-room problem is not yet localized to the refrigeration circuit
items.short_meaning: Reasonable suction and head for the current state/load shift attention toward airflow, infiltration/load, sensing/controls and available capacity.

items.relationship: Verified low evaporator load can lower evaporating pressure without proving low charge or a feed restriction.

steps.action: Confirm room/load condition, measure superheat, and evaluate liquid-supply/restriction evidence before diagnosing refrigerant starvation.
steps.record: Do not diagnose low charge from low suction alone.

items.heading: Low suction may be load-related rather than a feed fault
items.short_meaning: Verified low evaporator load can lower evaporating pressure without proving low charge or a feed restriction.

items.relationship: High current with normal head is not explained by excessive condensing pressure alone.

steps.action: Verify supply voltage/phase condition, compare current with nameplate, check start/run components where applicable, compressor temperature/protection and mechanical condition.
steps.record: Do not blame high head when head pressure is normal.

items.heading: High compressor current needs electrical/mechanical isolation
items.short_meaning: High current with normal head is not explained by excessive condensing pressure alone.

items.relationship: After a long off-cycle, suction and other readings can be transient while load and refrigerant distribution normalize.

steps.action: Confirm compressor/fans are operating, allow stable cooling, then remeasure suction, head, superheat and subcooling before diagnosing.
steps.record: Do not diagnose compressor inefficiency from startup suction alone.

items.heading: Startup pressure is not yet a steady-state diagnosis
items.short_meaning: After a long off-cycle, suction and other readings can be transient while load and refrigerant distribution normalize.

items.relationship: When cooling is satisfied/off, pressure behavior is not interpreted with steady-cooling diagnostic patterns.

steps.action: Wait for a cooling call and stable operation, then remeasure suction before diagnosing charge or feed.
steps.record: Do not diagnose low charge from an off-cycle suction reading.

items.heading: Off-cycle suction is not a steady-cooling diagnostic
items.short_meaning: When cooling is satisfied/off, pressure behavior is not interpreted with steady-cooling diagnostic patterns.

items.relationship: A hot compressor after a long off-cycle/startup raises migration/liquid-return and protection concerns that should be checked before repeated starts.

steps.action: Check crankcase heater/off-cycle protection and observe startup for liquid-return evidence before repeated starts.
steps.record: Do not repeatedly restart a compressor with suspected liquid slugging.

items.heading: Startup/migration history requires compressor-protection checks
items.short_meaning: A hot compressor after a long off-cycle/startup raises migration/liquid-return and protection concerns that should be checked before repeated starts.

items.relationship: Heat added during defrost can temporarily raise load and pressures during recovery.

steps.action: Trend pressures through recovery and diagnose only if abnormal values persist after the system returns to stable cooling.
steps.record: Do not diagnose overcharge from transient post-defrost high head.

items.heading: Post-defrost pressure transient requires stabilization
items.short_meaning: Heat added during defrost can temporarily raise load and pressures during recovery.

items.relationship: An active anti-short-cycle delay can intentionally hold the compressor off even while cooling demand exists.

steps.action: Verify the configured delay, allow it to expire, and confirm the compressor starts afterward.
steps.record: Do not bypass the delay or condemn the compressor while the delay is active.

items.heading: Compressor off-time delay is intentionally preventing restart
items.short_meaning: An active anti-short-cycle delay can intentionally hold the compressor off even while cooling demand exists.

items.relationship: Both a localized liquid-line restriction and incorrect TXV bulb contact can contribute to evaporator starvation/high superheat.

steps.action: Correct the drier restriction and bulb mounting, then stabilize and remeasure before judging charge.
steps.record: Do not add refrigerant before correcting the known restriction and bulb fault.

items.heading: Two starvation causes are directly observed
items.short_meaning: Both a localized liquid-line restriction and incorrect TXV bulb contact can contribute to evaporator starvation/high superheat.

items.relationship: With refrigeration performance verified normal, a sensor error can make the control respond to incorrect temperature information.

steps.action: Compare the sensor with an independent reference, inspect placement/wiring, and calibrate or replace as appropriate.
steps.record: Do not open the refrigerant circuit when refrigeration performance is verified normal.

items.heading: Control/sensing problem is favored over refrigerant fault
items.short_meaning: With refrigeration performance verified normal, a sensor error can make the control respond to incorrect temperature information.

items.relationship: A correctly operating refrigeration system cannot maintain the target when verified load exceeds available equipment capacity.

steps.action: Quantify actual load and equipment rated capacity; reduce load or correct equipment sizing/design rather than adjusting charge.
steps.record: Do not add refrigerant to fix an undersized system.

items.heading: Cooling load exceeds available system capacity
items.short_meaning: A correctly operating refrigeration system cannot maintain the target when verified load exceeds available equipment capacity.

items.relationship: A wet moisture indicator can identify contamination risk before obvious cooling performance is lost.

steps.action: Verify the indicator and service history; correct the moisture source and service the drier/evacuation as appropriate.
steps.record: Do not ignore a wet moisture indicator merely because temperatures are currently normal.

items.heading: Moisture contamination requires service attention even if cooling appears normal
items.short_meaning: A wet moisture indicator can identify contamination risk before obvious cooling performance is lost.

items.relationship: Uneven evaporator feed with proper liquid at the TXV inlet shifts attention to distributor/nozzle/circuit restriction or valve/feed application.

steps.action: Compare circuit temperatures and inspect distributor/nozzle and TXV application/feeding before adjusting charge.
steps.record: Do not diagnose low total charge solely from an uneven frost pattern.

items.heading: Evaporator distribution/feed problem needs localization
items.short_meaning: Uneven evaporator feed with proper liquid at the TXV inlet shifts attention to distributor/nozzle/circuit restriction or valve/feed application.

items.relationship: With head pressure not excessive, overheating may involve electrical supply/current, high compression ratio or low suction, return-gas cooling, protection history or internal problems.

steps.action: Check voltage/current, suction and compression ratio, return-gas conditions and overload history.
steps.record: Do not assume condenser/high head is the cause when head is not excessive.

items.heading: Compressor overheating needs causes beyond high head
items.short_meaning: With head pressure not excessive, overheating may involve electrical supply/current, high compression ratio or low suction, return-gas cooling, protection history or internal problems.

items.relationship: Low suction is consistent with verified low evaporator load; the evaporator airflow path is normal because the coil is clear and the fan is running.

steps.action: Confirm room/load condition and compare suction pressure with the expected low-load operating condition before diagnosing a feed or charge fault.
steps.record: Airflow path is normal; low suction alone is not proof of low charge.

items.heading: Low suction is consistent with low evaporator load
items.short_meaning: Verified low load can lower suction while the evaporator airflow path remains normal.

items.relationship: A confirmed refrigerant leak together with high superheat and low subcooling supports refrigerant loss/low charge.

steps.action: Repair the leak, leak-test as required, evacuate and charge by the approved manufacturer method, then verify stable superheat and subcooling.
steps.record: Correct the leak before final charge verification.

items.heading: Confirmed refrigerant leak supports a low-charge condition
items.short_meaning: The combined evidence supports refrigerant loss rather than a single-reading guess.

items.relationship: High ambient and high refrigeration load can elevate condensing pressure without proving a refrigerant fault.

steps.action: Record actual ambient and load, then compare condensing pressure and compressor operation with the manufacturer/application operating envelope for those conditions.
steps.record: Do not diagnose overcharge from high head alone.

items.heading: High head may be load/ambient driven rather than a fault
items.short_meaning: Both condenser ambient and refrigeration load are elevated.

items.relationship: Startup after a long off-cycle can carry migration and transient liquid-return risk; low superheat during this transient is not yet a steady-state charge diagnosis.

steps.action: Monitor compressor suction superheat and liquid-return indicators through startup; verify crankcase heater/migration protection and approved charge practices.
steps.record: Reassess after the system stabilizes.

items.heading: Startup after a long off-cycle carries migration/liquid-return risk
items.short_meaning: Transient liquid return can occur at startup and should be evaluated before steady-state diagnosis.

items.relationship: Low suction while satisfied/off is not interpreted as a running steady-cooling diagnosis.

steps.action: Confirm cooling demand; if diagnosis is needed, operate the system in cooling and obtain pressures/temperatures after stabilization.
steps.record: Do not apply steady-cooling pressure patterns to an off-cycle reading.

items.heading: Low suction while satisfied/off is not a cooling diagnosis
items.short_meaning: Off-cycle pressures are not interpreted like running steady-state pressures.

items.relationship: Low superheat with suction high for load and normal evaporator airflow forms an evaporator overfeed/flooding pattern.

steps.action: Verify TXV bulb mounting/insulation, valve setting and response, and actual evaporator load before making refrigerant-charge changes.
steps.record: Normal airflow reduces airflow restriction as the explanation.

items.heading: Evaporator overfeed/flooding pattern is present
items.short_meaning: With airflow not limiting load, the combination supports overfeeding or excess feed.

items.relationship: The evaporator is iced while the fan operates normally and defrost is incomplete, localizing attention to the defrost sequence rather than fan airflow hardware.

steps.action: Observe a complete defrost and verify heater output/current, defrost duration and termination.
steps.record: Evaporator fan operation is confirmed.

items.heading: Defrost is not fully clearing the evaporator
items.short_meaning: Persistent ice with the evaporator fan operating points to incomplete defrost.

items.relationship: Confirmed door infiltration adds warm humid air and latent load that can drive evaporator frost/icing even with the fan running.

steps.action: Repair the door/gasket/closure infiltration source, completely defrost the coil, then monitor the frost pattern for recurrence.
steps.record: Do not ignore the confirmed moisture load.

items.heading: Air infiltration is adding moisture that drives evaporator icing
items.short_meaning: Warm humid air entering the box increases latent load and frost formation.

items.relationship: With the door sealed and evaporator fan running, common infiltration and fan-failure causes are reduced; defrost performance and evaporating/feed conditions remain candidates.

steps.action: Observe defrost performance and termination; after the coil is clear, verify evaporating temperature, suction/feed and frost pattern during stable cooling.
steps.record: Do not stop at a generic icing diagnosis.

items.heading: Common airflow/infiltration causes are excluded; inspect defrost and evaporating condition
items.short_meaning: Defrost schedule/termination, low evaporating temperature or feed conditions remain candidates.

items.relationship: An LP control that opens while cooling demand remains may be opening above the intended cutout or responding to a genuine low-suction condition.

steps.action: Measure suction pressure accurately and compare actual LP cutout/cut-in with the equipment control sequence; correct the setting/control fault as required and verify restart.
steps.record: Verify the cause of low suction before adjusting a safety/control.

items.heading: LP control setting/fault may stop cooling prematurely
items.short_meaning: Verify actual pressure and intended cutout/cut-in before adjustment.

items.relationship: Two confirmed airflow faults are active: loss of evaporator airflow is an immediate cooling fault and the dirty condenser is a separate heat-rejection fault.

steps.action: Restore evaporator fan operation, clean the condenser, then retest room temperature, pressures and temperatures under stable cooling.
steps.record: Preserve both confirmed faults; do not erase the secondary condenser problem.

items.heading: Two confirmed airflow faults are active and both must be preserved
items.short_meaning: Evaporator airflow and condenser heat rejection both require correction.

items.relationship: Heat rejection, sensing and load problems are simultaneously present and can independently contribute to poor temperature control.

steps.action: Clean/restore condenser heat rejection, verify room temperature with a reference and correct the sensor issue, characterize product load, then reassess cooling.
steps.record: Do not select one contributor and discard the others.

items.heading: Heat rejection, sensing and load problems are simultaneously present
items.short_meaning: Multiple independent contributors can coexist.

items.relationship: An LP control trip while cooling demand remains may stop refrigeration prematurely if the cutout/setting, sensing line or control calibration is wrong.

steps.action: Measure actual suction/cutout pressure, compare LP cut-in/cutout with the application specification, and inspect the sensing line/control calibration before adjustment or replacement.
steps.record: Do not add refrigerant merely to keep an incorrectly set LP control closed.

items.heading: LP control setting/operation may be preventing adequate cooling
items.short_meaning: Verify actual trip pressure against the intended control setting and application.

items.relationship: High superheat and sight-glass bubbles without confirmed stable cooling can be transient and should not establish charge.

steps.action: Confirm stable cooling, then repeat superheat, liquid condition and applicable subcooling before diagnosing charge.
steps.record: Record operating state and repeat readings under stable cooling.

items.heading: Abnormal readings recorded but operating state must be established first
items.short_meaning: High superheat and sight-glass bubbles without confirmed stable cooling can be transient and should not establish charge.

items.relationship: Direct leak evidence outweighs indirect charge indicators; correct the leak before final charge assessment.

steps.action: Repair the leak, evacuate and charge by the equipment procedure, then verify stable operation and charge indicators.
steps.record: Record leak repair, evacuation/charging method and stabilized verification.

items.heading: Confirmed refrigerant leak requires repair before final charge verification
items.short_meaning: Direct leak evidence outweighs indirect charge indicators; correct the leak before final charge assessment.

items.relationship: Internally inconsistent head-pressure evidence must be verified before diagnosing a cause.

steps.action: Verify gauge/transducer accuracy, measurement point, refrigerant P-T conversion and operating state.
steps.record: Record corrected pressure/temperature and measurement location.

items.heading: High-head report conflicts with verified non-excessive head context
items.short_meaning: Internally inconsistent head-pressure evidence must be verified before diagnosing a cause.

items.relationship: High compressor current with low head points to electrical/mechanical loading rather than condenser overload.

steps.action: Verify supply voltage/unbalance, start/run components where applicable, compressor temperature and winding/mechanical condition.
steps.record: Record voltage, current, compressor temperature and electrical checks.

items.heading: High current is not explained by high condensing pressure
items.short_meaning: High compressor current with low head points to electrical/mechanical loading rather than condenser overload.

items.relationship: The pump-down sequence intentionally pulls suction pressure down after the liquid solenoid closes.

steps.action: Verify the low-pressure control opens at its intended cutout and the compressor stops; do not interpret pump-down suction as steady cooling.
steps.record: Record LP cutout and compressor stop behavior.

items.heading: Low suction is expected during pump-down
items.short_meaning: The pump-down sequence intentionally pulls suction pressure down after the liquid solenoid closes.

items.relationship: Sensor disagreement with otherwise normal refrigeration performance localizes the complaint to sensing/location/calibration.

steps.action: Verify sensor placement, calibration, wiring and controller input before refrigerant work.
steps.record: Record reference temperature and controller sensor reading.

items.heading: Temperature-control problem is localized to sensing rather than refrigeration capacity
items.short_meaning: Sensor disagreement with otherwise normal refrigeration performance localizes the complaint to sensing/location/calibration.

items.relationship: High subcooling and proper liquid at the TXV make simple low refrigerant inventory less likely; investigate feed/control and load.

steps.action: Check TXV response, bulb/equalizer and evaporator load before changing charge.
steps.record: Record valve response, bulb/equalizer condition and load.

items.heading: High superheat with retained liquid inventory points away from simple low charge
items.short_meaning: High subcooling and proper liquid at the TXV make simple low refrigerant inventory less likely; investigate feed/control and load.

items.relationship: The identified inlet restriction localizes the uneven-feed problem at/upstream of the expansion device.

steps.action: Inspect, clean or replace the inlet screen/orifice and verify solid liquid supply before retesting.
steps.record: Record inlet restriction correction and feed pattern.

items.heading: Localized TXV inlet restriction can produce uneven or starved feed
items.short_meaning: The identified inlet restriction localizes the uneven-feed problem at/upstream of the expansion device.

items.relationship: Low suction and high superheat can increase compression ratio and discharge temperature.

steps.action: Correct the cause of low suction/starvation, then verify compressor operating envelope and discharge temperature.
steps.record: Record stabilized suction, superheat, compression ratio and discharge temperature.

items.heading: Compressor thermal stress accompanies low-suction starved operation
items.short_meaning: Low suction and high superheat can increase compression ratio and discharge temperature.

items.relationship: High condensing pressure increases compression work and can contribute to high discharge temperature.

steps.action: Correct the high-head cause first, then recheck current, compression ratio and discharge temperature.
steps.record: Record heat-rejection correction and stabilized compressor values.

items.heading: High-side load is contributing to compressor thermal stress
items.short_meaning: High condensing pressure increases compression work and can contribute to high discharge temperature.

items.relationship: Low ambient may reduce liquid pressure enough to create flash gas or feeding problems when head-pressure control is absent or ineffective.

steps.action: Verify whether head-pressure control is required and present, then check liquid condition at the metering device.
steps.record: Record ambient, condensing pressure, head-control configuration and liquid condition.

items.heading: Low ambient can drive low condensing pressure
items.short_meaning: Low ambient may reduce liquid pressure enough to create flash gas or feeding problems when head-pressure control is absent or ineffective.

items.relationship: A normalized pressure does not explain the prior safety trip; an intermittent airflow, load or control event may have occurred.

steps.action: Review condenser fan operation, blockage/recirculation, ambient/load and reset/trip history before simply resetting.
steps.record: Record trip history and intermittent heat-rejection checks.

items.heading: High-pressure trip history needs cause investigation even though head is now normal
items.short_meaning: A normalized pressure does not explain the prior safety trip; an intermittent airflow, load or control event may have occurred.

items.relationship: Incorrect setpoint or differential can mimic refrigeration underperformance when the refrigeration circuit is normal.

steps.action: Correct setpoint/differential per application and observe temperature control before mechanical service.
steps.record: Record corrected settings and resulting control cycle.

items.heading: Control setting explains the temperature complaint
items.short_meaning: Incorrect setpoint or differential can mimic refrigeration underperformance when the refrigeration circuit is normal.

items.relationship: The evaporator is iced even though the fan runs, and defrost does not fully clear the coil.

steps.action: Check defrost duration, heater output and termination before charge adjustments.
steps.record: Record heater output, duration and termination behavior.

items.heading: Inadequate defrost is supported
items.short_meaning: The evaporator is iced even though the fan runs, and defrost does not fully clear the coil.

items.relationship: Post-defrost fan delay with a temporarily warm room may be normal sequence behavior until the coil is ready for airflow.

steps.action: Confirm the fan starts at the configured delay/temperature and room temperature then recovers.
steps.record: Record fan release point and room-temperature recovery.

items.heading: Intentional fan delay can temporarily delay room cooling after defrost
items.short_meaning: Post-defrost fan delay with a temporarily warm room may be normal sequence behavior until the coil is ready for airflow.

items.relationship: A bad sensor/control input can keep cooling demand active unnecessarily even when coils are clear.

steps.action: Verify sensor calibration/location and controller cutout behavior.
steps.record: Record sensor/reference comparison and controller cutout.

items.heading: Control or sensor error can cause excessive compressor runtime
items.short_meaning: A bad sensor/control input can keep cooling demand active unnecessarily even when coils are clear.

items.relationship: Liquid flow continuing with the solenoid commanded closed prevents normal pump-down.

steps.action: Verify the valve de-energizes and inspect or repair the leaking solenoid seat.
steps.record: Record valve command, voltage and actual flow.

items.heading: Leaking liquid solenoid defeats pump-down
items.short_meaning: Liquid flow continuing with the solenoid commanded closed prevents normal pump-down.

items.relationship: Confirmed infiltration and sensor error are independent room-side faults and both must be preserved.

steps.action: Repair infiltration and verify sensor/reference accuracy before refrigerant adjustments.
steps.record: Record door/gasket correction and sensor comparison.

items.heading: Both infiltration and sensing faults can affect room control
items.short_meaning: Confirmed infiltration and sensor error are independent room-side faults and both must be preserved.

items.relationship: Evaporator fan failure and dirty condenser can distort refrigerant readings; high superheat should be reassessed after correction.

steps.action: Restore evaporator fan operation and clean the condenser, then stabilize and repeat superheat and pressures.
steps.record: Preserve both direct faults and record stabilized readings.

items.heading: Direct airflow faults on both sides make superheat secondary until corrected
items.short_meaning: Evaporator fan failure and dirty condenser can distort refrigerant readings; high superheat should be reassessed after correction.

items.relationship: Drier restriction evidence and TXV bulb fault can coexist and mimic charge problems.

steps.action: Correct the drier restriction and bulb mounting, then reassess charge indicators.
steps.record: Do not add refrigerant before correcting localized faults.

items.heading: Two localized feed faults are present; low subcooling should not erase them
items.short_meaning: Drier restriction evidence and TXV bulb fault can coexist and mimic charge problems.

items.relationship: A command-versus-response solenoid fault is direct evidence and does not require steady-state pressure inference.

steps.action: Inspect the solenoid and pressure differential and restore flow before broader diagnosis.
steps.record: Record coil voltage, pressure differential and restored flow.

items.heading: Direct liquid-solenoid flow fault is actionable even if overall state is uncertain
items.short_meaning: A command-versus-response solenoid fault is direct evidence and does not require steady-state pressure inference.

items.relationship: A direct room-load fault should not be hidden by missing operating-state information.

steps.action: Repair infiltration, then establish stable cooling and reassess the remaining temperature complaint.
steps.record: Record infiltration correction and stabilized room response.

items.heading: Confirmed infiltration remains actionable with unknown refrigeration state
items.short_meaning: A direct room-load fault should not be hidden by missing operating-state information.

items.relationship: Do not use defrost pressure as steady-state charge evidence; preserve the physical condenser fault.

steps.action: Clean the condenser and repeat pressures only after defrost ends and stable cooling resumes.
steps.record: Record condenser correction and stabilized pressure.

items.heading: Defrost makes refrigerant readings transient, but dirty condenser remains a direct fault
items.short_meaning: Do not use defrost pressure as steady-state charge evidence; preserve the physical condenser fault.

items.relationship: Transient post-defrost superheat should not distract from a direct moisture/load fault.

steps.action: Repair infiltration and repeat superheat after stable cooling is restored.
steps.record: Record infiltration correction and stabilized superheat.

items.heading: Post-defrost superheat is transient while confirmed infiltration remains actionable
items.short_meaning: Transient post-defrost superheat should not distract from a direct moisture/load fault.
